dct_description_sm: Caribou and moose are an important traditional and cultural resource for northern communities, and important traditional food species.  Tracking levels of environmental contaminants is important to help support and maintain public confidence in caribou and moose as healthy and important food choices.  Given recent declines in caribou populations in northern Canada, it is also important to track contaminant levels as part of overall herd monitoring programs.  Caribou rely heavily on lichen as part of their winter diet, and lichen can accumulate atmospheric contaminants in a non-selective manner.  As a result of their diet, long-lived species like caribou can accumulate some elements over time.  Elevated levels of cadmium have been found in caribou and moose in some areas of the Canadian and circumpolar north.  During the 1990's, extensive contaminants testing was done in caribou herds across northern Canada.  Since that time, several 'sentinel' herds have been monitored to track changes in contaminant levels, but it is also important to periodically re-test the other herds as well.  Similarly, it is important to establish baseline levels of key metals in moose and track them over time.
dct_title_s: Heavy Metal Contaminants in Caribou and Moose, Northwest Territories
